Valor Frontier

Audio combat · blind accessible

Valor Frontier

For the full experience: play in landscape with your screen reader on and headphones in. Landscape puts Turn left, Fire and Turn right side by side, your screen reader speaks every callout, and headphones let you hear which side enemies are coming from. Playing without a screen reader? Set Announcements to Built-in voice in Settings. Blind and playing with your screen reader off? Hold two fingers still on any menu for two seconds to turn on the Menu reader, which reads the menus aloud.

A shooter you play by ear. Enemies close in from every direction. Listen for where they are, turn to face them, and fire when you hear the lock-on ping.

Checking your saved progress…

Play together

Co-op

Team up with one friend online, anywhere in the world. You stand back to back on the same battlefield against the same enemies, each with your own weapons, armor and upgrades. Play Campaign, Endless survival, Boss rush or Zombie siege. Zombie siege works in Standard, Watch my six and Ragdoll sandbox, with all of its Advanced options, and each of you gets your own perk machine. Horror hallway is solo only. There are more enemies, and they are tougher. You both earn silver for every kill. You hear your teammate's gunfire from the direction they are facing, and Status tells you their health. If either of you falls, the battle ends for both of you. Pausing pauses it for both of you.

    Training

    How to fight

    The sound check is further down this page. Each enemy button lists its health and what to expect.

    Where enemies are. Each enemy makes its own sound, panned left or right. Sounds behind you are muffled and dull. Louder means closer.

    Aiming. Turn left and turn right rotate you 15 degrees. About face spins you all the way around. When an enemy is in your sights you hear a fast high ping. Closer enemies ping higher. The ping sounds the same on every map, and the background ambience dips while something is in your sights so the ping stays clear. You can raise it with the Lock-on ping volume slider in Settings. Facing north plays a bright two-note chime.

    Range. Battlefields are big. Enemies appear close, at mid-range, or far off, up to about 160 feet away, and every enemy is announced with its distance in feet. Far-off enemies sound quieter and duller. Pistols and submachine guns are only fully effective to about 40 feet, except the MP5, which reaches about 65 feet, the MAC-10, only about 30, and the Gyrojet rocket pistol, which works the other way: weak up close and stronger the farther the rocket flies, hardest at its 70-foot limit, and rifles to about 85 to 100 feet; past that they lose damage and accuracy. Shotguns lose power past about 23 feet, and their blast also hurts enemies standing within 10 feet of the one you hit. Hollow point rounds hit much harder within 25 feet but weaker far away. Sniper rifles never lose damage, so they are the tool for long shots. Any round that punches through enemies, like the anti-tank rifle, the Jet rifle, or the M249 with armor piercing rounds, never loses damage to distance either. Attacking enemies are about 4 feet from you.

    Headshots. When the lock-on ping turns into a double chirp, the enemy is dead centre. Shots then land as headshots for 60 percent more damage, 30 percent on bosses, with a crisp crack on impact. A reflex sight makes headshots hit much harder. A sniper scope turns most long-range hits into headshots. With both Ramjet ammo upgrades on, a Jet rifle headshot hits for 10,000. A precision scope makes sniper headshots hit far harder and almost every sniper shot land. A grip widens the dead-centre zone and turns some off-centre hits into headshots. Shotguns cannot headshot unless they have a grip.

    Enemy locations reads out the enemies by clock position, distance in feet and health percent, nearest first. 12 o'clock is straight ahead, 3 o'clock is to your right, 6 o'clock is behind you. To keep big waves short, enemies at the same clock position and within 5 feet of each other are read as one group, like 5 Zombie runners, 2 o'clock, 50 to 54 feet, average health 80 percent. A group of mixed types says what is in it, like 7 zombies, 2 o'clock, 50 to 54 feet: 6 Zombie runners and 1 Zombie. Bosses, mini bosses and mega enemies are always read on their own. With more than 8 groups, the nearest 8 are read in full, plus any boss, and the rest are summed up by direction, like Farther out: 12 at 12 o'clock. After you wound an enemy you also hear its health percent.

    Hits and misses. Every bullet that lands makes a short thud from where the enemy is: a soft thud on people and wolves, a metallic tink on drones and mechs, a deep heavy thud on armored brutes, raiders and bosses. A bullet zipping past the enemy means you missed it. A distant ricochet or dirt puff means nothing was there.

    Reloading. Guns reload by themselves the moment the magazine runs dry, and when you switch to an empty gun. Press Reload any time to top up early.

    Holding fire. Tap Fire for one trigger pull. To keep firing, press and hold the Fire button. With VoiceOver, double-tap and hold. On a keyboard, hold Space. A faint tick on each shot means your magazine is running low.

    Fire lock. The small Fire lock switch in the very top right corner of the battle screen keeps your gun firing on its own, so you can turn left and right freely while you shoot. Press it once for Fire lock on, and again for Fire lock off. On a keyboard, press L. It keeps firing through reloads, and on guns that overheat it waits out the cooldown and starts again. It stays on while you are paused. It turns off when you switch weapons, when you die, when the match ends, or when you press and let go of the Fire button. It does nothing with melee weapons.

    Menu reader. For playing with your screen reader off. Turn it on in Settings, or hold two fingers still on any menu for two seconds. The Built-in voice then reads the menus, the Armory, Settings, the pause menu and every other screen outside of battle. Touch or drag a finger to hear what is under it. Swipe right or left for the next or previous item. Double-tap anywhere to press the item you last heard. Swipe up or down to change a slider or picker, or to jump between headings. Drag two fingers to scroll. In a text box, double-tap to type, each letter is spoken as you type it, and double-tap again when you are done. The battle screen itself still works by direct touch.

    Co-op. The Co-op button on the main menu teams you up with one friend anywhere in the world. One of you creates a room and gets a 5 number code, and the other joins with it. You stand back to back against the same enemies, each with your own weapons and upgrades, in Campaign, Endless survival, Boss rush and Zombie siege.

    Cover. Take cover halves the damage you take, but your aim gets shakier and the battle sounds muffled. Leave cover to aim steady again. Bosses roar as they wind up a big attack: that is your cue to take cover. The Iron Revenant fires rockets from range, so listen for the whistle.

    Grenades go off around you, so there is no aiming. Frag grenades blast every enemy within 5 feet, perfect when enemies are attacking you. Cryo grenades freeze every enemy within 8 feet to about a third of their speed for 8 seconds. Incendiary grenades are the opposite: a whoomp of flame hits every enemy within 15 feet for 30 and sets them on fire until they die, and a ring of fire roars all around you for 15 seconds, setting alight anything that comes within 15 feet. Any burning enemy roars and crackles with fire from where it stands for as long as it burns. The Fat Man destroys everything within 50 feet instantly, bosses included, after a falling whistle. A jack-in-the-box is a proximity bomb: it sits 10 feet in front of you playing a little music-box tune, and when an enemy comes within 7 feet of it, the lid pops with a boing and it explodes, hitting everything within 15 feet of the box. An event horizon is a gravity trap: it sits 10 feet in front of you giving off a slow, deep double pulse. When any enemy comes within 13 feet of you, from any side, it switches on with a warbling energy charge that wobbles faster and faster, then snaps into a deep roar, then for one minute it drags every enemy that comes within 13 feet of you into a tight cluster around itself and holds them there, with a throbbing hum. Held enemies cannot move or attack, and it does no damage, so line them up and open fire. Three quick beeps mean it fades in 10 seconds. Paradox Pandora's Box creaks open at your feet and a shuffle of chimes rolls like a spinning wheel, then one of 9 effects, picked completely at random, hits every enemy within 30 feet, and a voice tells you which. Each has its own sound. Inferno, a whoomp of fire: everything burns until it dies. Teleport, warbling swoops: each enemy vanishes with a falling zap and pops back in where it spawned. Deep freeze, an icy burst and chimes: frozen solid for one minute. Mass hypnosis, a rising two-note spiral: they fight for you. Lovestruck, a harp and a heartbeat: they wander harmlessly for 30 seconds. Munchies, a crunch and a dopey groan: dazed and harmless for good. Reverse gravity, a rising whoosh: they float upside down, helpless, for about 5 seconds, then crash down with a thud for 40 percent of their health. Shrink, a rising zap and squeaks: tiny, squeaky, 1 health left and weak little attacks. Slow motion, a sound like a tape slowing down: a tenth of their speed for 30 seconds, their voices slowed right down, and the tape speeds back up when it wears off. Bosses, mega bosses and the Ancient One cannot be hypnotized, lovestruck or dazed, take only 10 percent from the reverse gravity crash, and shrink to half size, losing half their health. In co-op and practice, hypnosis, lovestruck and munchies are left out. None of them hurt you. Grenade type cycles between all seven.

    Modes. Campaign is five waves ending in the battlefield's boss. Endless survival never stops, brings a boss every fifth wave and a mega boss with twice a boss's health every seventh wave, and pays a bonus for every wave you clear. Boss rush is only bosses: it starts with one weakened boss and gets brutal far faster than endless, with a mega boss every seventh wave. Tutorial/practice is a guided tutorial with three levels, chosen from the Tutorial level dropdown under Mode: Basic info teaches every button, Intermediate learner introduces every enemy, and Battle scholar teaches any 4 weapons you pick plus every grenade. Each instruction is spoken and waits for you to do it. Afterwards targets keep coming so you can practice. Targets stand still and cannot hurt you. Zombie siege is endless waves of the undead. Four glass windows surround you about 50 feet out, at north, east, south and west. A zombie has to smash through a window to reach you, which takes a few seconds: you hear banging and cracking glass from that direction, then a crash when it shatters. Broken windows seal themselves again 15 seconds later. Every fifth wave brings a giant zombie boss, and every tenth wave also brings a mega giant zombie boss with five times a giant's health, paying five times a giant's silver, so waves 10, 20, 30 and so on have both. Every 50th wave, in every zombie mode, the Ancient One awakens: the ultimate zombie boss. The first one has 10,000 health on every difficulty, and each one after it has 2,500 more, hitting harder and paying more silver in step. It wakes with a deafening roar that shakes the ground, and keeps roaring every few seconds. In Giants only, there is just the mega giant every tenth wave. The horde grows every wave, to about 200 zombies by wave 50, and there is no limit on how many can be after you at once, so the whole wave can be alive together. After every 50 zombies come in there is a short breather before the next ones: 6 seconds on Normal spawning, 4 and a half on Fast, 3 on Faster and 1 and a half on Hyperspeed. Zombies hit softer than soldiers and pay 20 percent less silver, but kills pay 8 percent more every wave. Status reads the state of every window. That is the Standard zombie mode. In Advanced options, the Giants only checkbox makes every zombie a giant zombie boss, in the same numbers as a normal wave, so by wave 50 you face about 200 giants, plus a mega giant every tenth wave. Giants only keeps its own best records.

    Watch my six. A zombie mode with only two windows: one straight ahead of you at 12 o'clock and one right behind you at 6 o'clock. Nothing comes from the left or right, so About face is your best friend.

    Horror hallway. A zombie mode where you walk down a long hallway on your own, with no walk button. Your footsteps tell you your pace: quick, close together steps when the hallway ahead is clear, slowing down the more zombies are ahead, until you stop completely. You also stop while a zombie is right in front of you or grabbing you. Zombies come straight out of the walls with no barriers, appearing 10 to 20 feet away, so react fast. They start a little slower than in other modes and get faster every wave, up to double speed around wave 25. Waves come one after another with only a short pause, so expect a steady flow. If you walk past one, it chases you from behind, fast, but never faster than double speed. A soft double tick plays every 100 feet. Your score is every foot you walk plus 10 points for every kill. Status reads your distance, kills and score.

    Jungle scavenger. A zombie mode on Verdant Hollow where you walk freely. The map is eight clearings joined by straight trails: Base camp in the middle, River crossing to the north and the Waterfall beyond it, Parrot tree to the east, Frog pond to the west, Crashed plane to the south, Stone ruins to the north east and Bamboo grove to the north west. Each trail is about 120 feet long, or about 170 feet for the diagonal ones. Every clearing has its own sound so you can tell where it is: a crackling campfire, running water, a roaring waterfall, parrot squawks, frog croaks, radio beeps, a hollow wind and bamboo knocks. To walk, hold and drag on the Turn left button: drag up to walk forward, down to back up, sideways to sidestep. To turn, hold and drag sideways on the Turn right button, and you turn one step for every short drag. Keep your finger held out to the side and you keep turning, faster the further out you hold it. Slide back towards where you started, or lift your finger, to stop. Fire is a strip across the top of the screen in this mode, and the two pads fill the area below it, walking on the left half and turning on the right half. A quick tap on either button still turns you one step. Dragging with two thumbs needs your screen reader off, with Announcements set to Built-in voice in Settings. With a screen reader on, use Turn left and Turn right as usual and press the Walk button, where Take cover normally is, to walk forward on your own, and press it again to stop. You hear your footsteps as you move, and they are loud enough to hear over any horde. Each direction sounds different: a firm boot step going forward, a toe drag then a heel going backward, a slide and a tap on the side you are sidestepping to, and a pivot scuff on the side you are turning to. You can leave the trails and push straight through the jungle, just like the zombies. Off the trails you walk at a bit over half speed and every footstep swishes through the undergrowth. The game says when you step off a trail and when you are back on one, and it says the name of each clearing as you arrive and each trail as you step onto it. The map ends about 65 feet beyond the outer clearings, where leaves brush against you and you can go no further. Zombies come through the jungle from every side, 70 to 115 feet away, and a zombie standing right in front of you blocks your way. Supply crates wait in the clearings and beep: two rising beeps for a medkit, three wooden clicks for a grenade crate, a coin chime for a silver cache. Walk onto a crate to collect it. A medkit restores 40 percent of your health, a grenade crate gives 2 grenades that you keep, and a silver cache pays 20 silver plus 10 for every wave. Clearing a wave does not heal you here, apart from your Field medic perk, but it drops two new crates, one of them always a medkit, and gives you 20 seconds to scavenge before the next wave. The Surroundings button reads where you are, which trails lead where, and where every crate is, with the trail to take. Off the trails it reads the nearest trail and the nearest clearing. There is no cover in this mode: when a giant winds up, back away.

    Perk machine. In every zombie mode, after you clear every fifth wave the perk machine opens with a music-box jingle. Perks cost silver and last for the rest of that run. Electric fence: an electrified band from 20 feet in to 14 feet around you. A zombie touching it makes a loud electric crack, then sharp zaps while it struggles through at 60 percent speed, taking damage every second. Weaker zombies usually fry, but tougher zombies in later waves get through hurt, and runners can dash across. Giant zombies take more damage but are not slowed. A soft hum every few seconds tells you the fence is on. The electric fence is not offered in Horror hallway, since you keep walking forward. Iron gut: 50 more maximum health. Quick hands: reloads twice as fast. Double tap: your shots hit 35 percent harder. Second wind: the first time you would fall, you get back up with half your health. Bloodthirst: every kill heals you 3 health, or 10 for a mini boss or boss. Gold rush: double silver for the rest of the run. Frost skin: any zombie that hits you is frozen for 2 seconds, bosses for 1. Last stand: when your health drops below a quarter, a shockwave hits every zombie within 15 feet for 150 damage and throws survivors back, once per wave. Growing Violence: your shots hit 10 percent harder for every wave after you buy it, added up flat, so plus 50 percent five waves later and double damage after ten. Status tells you how high it has climbed.

    Mythical weapons. Thunderclap chains lightning: listen for crackles jumping between enemies. Thunderclap upgrades: a static field makes shocked enemies buzz and move at half speed, the ball lightning slug fires a fizzing orb straight ahead that passes through up to 7 enemies, scorches anyone within 2 feet of them and bursts into chain lightning, and when the lightning rod is charged you hear a rising hum and then electricity crackling around you until you fire your supercharged blast with its long deep rumble. The Black Hole Cannon's orb hums where it lands, drags enemies toward it, then collapses with a boom. The Banshee's scream hits and stuns everything in front of you, and stunned enemies make a ringing sound. It is strongest within 40 feet and weakens out to 160 feet. The Hydra's three rockets each explode where their target is, so you hear up to three blasts in different places, or six with Severed heads. High explosive shells land with a bigger, deeper, rolling blast. Corrosive shells land with a wet splat and a hiss, splashing acid onto anyone within 2 feet, and enemies covered in acid fizz and smoke every second until it fades after 10 seconds. With Corrosive shells V2, a bubbling, popping sound is an acid pool on the ground: anything walking through it sizzles, and the bubbling stops after 7 seconds when the pool dries up. The Alien Symbiote fires wet, fleshy bursts. It only feeds when you use it: every kill it makes eats 2 of your maximum health and makes it stronger, at 40 percent more damage for every 50 health eaten. Now and then you hear it feed, a squelch, a growl and a heartbeat, and you hear its damage each time it passes another whole multiple. It is fully grown at 600 damage per second, or 2400 with Feeding frenzy, or when your maximum health is down to 100. Status tells you how strong it has grown. Carrying it without using it never costs you health. With vampiric rounds, every kill it makes gives you back 2 health with a soft heartbeat pulse. With Hair trigger V2, the Banshee becomes a tactical rifle: each trigger pull is a tight burst of 3 quick shrieks that hit harder, with a short pause between bursts. The Jack Frost chills hard: each icicle slows an enemy more, down to a tenth of its speed after four hits. Its Blizzard blast goes off when you reload: a whirling wind storm circles you, then a crunch of ice as every enemy within 40 feet freezes completely still for 15 seconds. Ice cracking means they are moving again, and a crystal chime means the next blizzard is ready, 10 seconds after the last. The Jet rifle's heat vent goes off with a roaring rush of hot air, bigger the more rounds you fired. With both Ramjet upgrades, a Jet round punches through every enemy in its line, with no limit, and never skips one, even from cover. The Dark Quasar Turbine roars like a jet engine for as long as you hold fire. Behind you, enemies are sucked into the intake and shredded with a grinding crunch, and a rising ping counts each one toward Quasar propulsion. In front of you, enemies are blown away by the exhaust and you hear them moving off into the distance. Fast beeping means it is about to overheat, a long hiss of steam means it has, quiet metal pings mean it is still cooling, and a two-note chime means it is ready again. After every 30 enemies sucked in, you hear a rising charge whine and then a huge laser blast fires straight ahead. With the Devourer beam, every enemy sucked in also fires a quick bright laser zap straight ahead, so a stream of zaps means the turbine is feeding well. The Hades Pump Action roars out a jet of fire and racks its pump after every shot. Enemies it hits crackle as they burn, and the fire never goes out until they die. The Lantern of Ra hums with a bright, shimmering chord for as long as you hold Fire, rising in pitch as it heats up, and every enemy it touches flares up with a burst of fire and then crackles as it burns. Volcanic slugs land with a deep boom and a gloopy sizzle as the enemy erupts. You hear every shell click in as it reloads, and the pump racks when it is full. The Tetra-prism sniper fires crystals that ring out like a struck crystal bowl. Every crystal that hits has a 15 percent chance, 24 with the Ruby spyglass, of a crystallizing headshot, wherever you aim: a racing crackle and a shimmering chord mean the enemy has been turned to crystal and is dead. Bosses and mini bosses get a lower, heavier version: they are locked in crystal for 3 seconds, silent and still, then burst out with a crack and a spray of shards. Crystal statues stay put until the next wave, then crumble into tinkling dust around you, and Status tells you how many are standing. Its Emerald implosion ability, which you use instead of Shattered glass, turns crystal statues into mines: when an enemy walks into one, you hear a rising, sucking crystal whirl as everything within 5 feet is dragged in for three quarters of a second, then a bright shattering boom as it bursts outward, hitting everything within 5 feet for 60 and throwing them like an explosion. Survivors are knocked down and get back up. A burst that reaches another mine sets it off too, so a field of statues can go off in a chain. The The Hypno-rifle is a mythical full auto assault rifle: about one round in four hypnotizes the enemy it hits, which then fights for you with triple health, damage and speed until it dies, with a soft two-note chime so you can hear where it is. Micro Catastrophe is a mythical pistol: a squeaky little pew, then a huge deep explosion with rumbling debris where the round lands, and every enemy within 50 feet is thrown. Supernova is a mythical heavy sniper rifle: every round hits for 900 and the star goes supernova, blasting everyone within 10 feet of the enemy hit for 250. Its Singularity implosion drags everything within 20 feet together and blasts them outward, and its Chain reaction makes every enemy the blast reaches explode too. Unbearable Buddy is a mythical toy: hold Fire and a buzzing laser beam pours out of both of its eyes. The buzz drops in pitch as the battery drains, two quick beeps mean the battery is low, and a power-down whine means it is flat. Changing the battery clicks the hatch open on the back of the bear's head, slides the old battery out and the new one in, and when it is done Unbearable Buddy speaks. With Blinding love, a rising harp and a heartbeat mean an enemy has been blinded by love: it wanders around for 30 seconds without attacking, and you hear a soft heartbeat where it is. A falling tone means it has snapped out of it. Brain Fog Bites is a bag of snacks: press Fire and you hear the bag crinkle as you throw a handful, then a crunchy scatter where it lands, at the nearest enemy you are facing up to 40 feet away, or 40 feet straight ahead. Enemies nearby go for the pile, and you hear crunchy munching as they eat. An enemy that has eaten enough gives a dopey, slowed down moan and is dazed for good: it wanders about, never attacks, and keeps moaning now and then so you can find it and finish it off.

    Silver and the Armory. Every kill pays silver: 10 for light enemies, 16 for heavy ones, 50 for mini bosses, 83 for bosses and 250 for mega bosses. In endless survival, boss rush and zombie siege, every kill pays 8 percent more silver for each wave you have survived, so wave 11 pays almost double. Every regular wave has one mini boss: it announces itself with a rising two-note siren before its cry, and it is far tougher than a normal enemy. Spend it in the Armory shop on weapons, attachments, body armor, grenades and perks. Toughness and Field medic go up to level 150, Deadeye and Scavenger up to level 50: Toughness for more health, Field medic for more healing between waves, Deadeye for more gun damage and Scavenger for more silver per kill. Kills also raise each gun's mastery, up to level 10, making its attachments stronger.

    Kinetic bat. A mythical high tech weapon in the Armory under Legendary, Mythical, High tech weapons. It does not count as a melee weapon. Press Fire to swing: a whoosh and a bright metal ping as the bat knocks a baseball at the nearest enemy you are facing. The ball is slow, so you hear it whistle out toward the enemy, and it follows the enemy if it moves. A leathery thock is the ball hitting, with the headshot crack if it hit a head. A springy rising zip means it bounced on to another enemy within 7 feet, and it keeps bouncing as long as there is one, for up to 15 seconds. A soft falling shimmer means its 15 seconds are up and it has faded away. Two or three dull bounces and a roll mean it hit the ground and is done, and you hear how many hits it made. With Fastball the whistle is higher and quicker. After each swing the bat needs 5 seconds to recharge, so you can hit one baseball every 5 seconds. Pressing Fire sooner tells you how long is left, and a two-note chime means it is ready. Status tells you how many baseballs are in play.

    Scavenger pack. The Razor blade boomerang is thrown with Fire. You hear Boomerang out, then its blades whirring as it leaves on your left, loops out across the front of you and curves back in on your right. A bright shing is an enemy being sliced, once on the way out and again on the way back. Pressing Fire while it is out just tells you it is still out, and you hear Boomerang returned when you catch it. Its Narrow arc and Full circle abilities change the path it flies. The Razorwire Carapace armor tears into anything that hits you: a ripping sound is the barbs, and wet dripping means the enemy is bleeding. With its Hungry barbs ability, every enemy the barbs kill makes them 10 percent stronger, up to triple damage after 20 barb kills in one battle. A rising metal scrape means they just got sharper.

    Ragdoll sandbox. A zombie mode that plays like Zombie siege, with four windows 50 feet out, but with real physics. Every zombie has a body with a head, arms and legs. When one dies it goes limp and flies the way it was hit: a pistol drops it, a shotgun or sniper rifle throws it, and explosions launch it, spinning, out across the room. Bodies tumble and slide along the floor, slam into the round wall, smash through windows or sail right over the wall, and pile up on top of each other. A body flying into a standing zombie knocks it flat. Blasts that do not kill a zombie throw it off its feet instead: it lies there for a second or two, then gets back up where it landed, so a well-placed grenade really does buy you room. Big explosions tear arms, legs and heads off. Everything makes a sound from where it happens: a rushing whoosh follows each of the fastest flying bodies, rising in pitch the faster it goes, then a low scrape if it slides along the floor. A heavy thump is a body hitting the floor, lighter slaps are arms and legs, and a big thump with a hollow knock is a body hitting the wall. Breaking glass is a body going through a window, which leaves it open for a few seconds. A crack and a wet tear is a limb coming off. An impact and a grunt is a body bowling over another zombie, and scuffling followed by a groan is a knocked-down zombie getting back up. Hydra acid pools eat through legs: a zombie that stands in one hears its shins froth away and drops to its knees, then loses its legs completely and slaps down onto its belly as a crawler. Crawlers drag themselves toward you at about a third of their speed, and each pull makes a slap and a wet scrape you can follow. While its legs are dissolving, a zombie takes very little damage from the pool, so you will hear it happen before it dies, and a crawler takes half damage from it. Enemy locations tells you which zombies are on their knees or crawling. Status tells you how many bodies are on the floor and how many zombies are knocked down. Sighted players see a simple first-person view inside the Fire button, with stick-figure zombies, the wall and windows around you, and the radar in the corner.

    Physics and picture in every mode. The ragdoll physics from Ragdoll sandbox now run in every mode: campaign, endless survival, boss rush, Tutorial/practice and every zombie mode. Every enemy has a body with a head, arms and legs, sized to the enemy, so a Mercenary goes down like a person, wolves, jaguars and the Mega Pigeon run on four legs, and bosses like Gargantuos Gargantar are huge, heavy bodies that take a big blast to move. Kills fly the way they were hit, explosions throw bodies and knock survivors off their feet, big blasts tear limbs off, flying bodies bowl over other enemies, and Hydra acid turns enemies into crawlers. You hear it all the same way as in Ragdoll sandbox: the whoosh of a flying body, thumps and slaps as it lands, and a scuffle as a knocked-down enemy gets back up. Zombies groan when they get up, other enemies grunt, and drones and mechs clank like metal when they hit the floor. Out in the open there is no wall, so bodies sail as far as they are thrown. In Horror hallway they slam into the hallway walls, and the bodies you leave behind slide away behind you as you walk. Status tells you how many bodies are on the floor and how many enemies are knocked down. Sighted players see the simple first-person view inside the Fire button in every mode, with each map's own sky and ground, colored figures for each enemy type, and the hallway walls in Horror hallway.

    Nightwalker pack. A legendary set in the Armory shop, under Legendary, with three sections: Machine guns, Scythes and Armor. Vlad the Impaler is a light machine gun that fires wooden stakes, one every second, from a belt of 100, or 150 with its Extended magazine. Each stake makes a heavy pneumatic thump and whistles away, with a wooden thock when it lands. A stake hits the first enemy for 10, and as a built-in trait a headshot does 2.5 times that, 25, on bosses too, with its own heavy chained slicing sound. If that kills it, the body is thrown 10 feet back. Any living enemy standing in those 10 feet behind it, in line with the shot, is skewered too and pinned to the body: up to 2 enemies at stock or with Blood crank, 3 enemies on one stake in all, or up to 5 with the Grindstone attachment, 6 in all. Each enemy down the stake takes 15 percent less than the one before: 10, then 8.5, 7.2, 6.1, 5.2 and 4.4. You hear a wet squelch when enemies are pinned together. Pinned enemies stay alive, keep coming and keep attacking, but they move as one clump at the speed of the slowest, until each one takes a fatal hit, and Enemy locations tells you who is pinned with how many others. With nobody behind it, the body is pinned to the floor with a deep thud, or to the wall with a hollow knock in the zombie window modes. Bosses are never pinned: they just fall over when it kills them, but other enemies can be pinned to a living boss. Abnormal agility halves its reload time. Grindstone slows it to one stake every 1.4 seconds. Blood crank instead speeds it up to one stake every 0.4 seconds, and you can only use one of the two. Stacking stakes works with either: every stake in an enemy makes the next one hit it 20 percent of full damage harder, 10, then 12, 14 and so on. The Unquenchable scythe is a melee weapon that swings in a full circle around you once every 2.7 seconds. You hear the blade whoosh around your head, starting straight ahead and sweeping right, behind you and left, and a slice as it hits each enemy. Everything within 10 feet takes 75, and every kill heals you 20 percent of that enemy's full health. Leeching edge also heals you 10 percent of every hit, and Bloodthirsty energy doubles its reach to 20 feet. You must own the Darkest Shadow Suit before you can buy it. The Darkest Shadow Suit cuts damage by 60 percent. Its Bat swarm ability charges from the damage you take while wearing it: every time it adds up to half your maximum health, 5 bats burst out with a flurry of wings and shrieks, and Bat swarm half charged tells you when you are halfway. They fly at 8 feet a second to the enemies closest to you, and you hear their wings and bites from wherever they are. Each bite does 3 and heals you 3. They stay out for 10 seconds, then fly off and the charge starts over. Endless appetite keeps them out for 15 seconds, and every kill they make has the whole swarm fly and bite 25 percent faster, with a rising triple chirp. All healing from the scythe and the bats is added up and announced every 1 and a half seconds, like Feeding +15 health. Status tells you how charged the bat swarm is, or how long the bats have left.

    Dark samurai. A special ability for the Samurai armor. It charges from the damage you take while wearing it, with a low snarl and Dark samurai half charged at an eighth of your max health. At a quarter of your max health a dark rift opens with a deep rumble, and two oni demons snarl at your left and right, then run out to attack. Listen for their snarls moving across the battlefield and the snapping bites when they hit. They go for the enemies closest to you first. After 25 seconds a falling hiss means they have vanished.

    Samurai pack. The Samurai sword is swung with Fire, one heavy swing a second: a ring of steel and a deep whoosh sweeping left to right. Anything within 5 feet straight in front of you is cut down instantly, with a slicing cleave, except bosses and mini bosses, which take 100. Every swing also sends a purple energy wave straight ahead. You hear it hum away from you, climbing in pitch as it grows stronger, and every enemy it passes through gives off a ghostly shimmer, brighter the harder it was hit. The wave starts 5 feet wide and spreads to 35 feet wide at its full reach of 35 feet, and the farther it travels the harder it hits: 100 at the blade, 1,000 at 35 feet. So enemies a little way off take the most. You must own the Samurai armor, which cuts the damage you take by 75 percent, before you can buy the sword.

    Switching freezes time. Switching weapon or grenade type stops the whole battle for 2 and a half seconds after your last press, so you can cycle through without being swarmed. Status and Enemy locations stop time too, for as long as it takes to read the whole thing to you. A falling whoosh means time has stopped and the battle sounds go quiet. Firing, turning, reloading, throwing a grenade or taking cover starts time again straight away, with a rising whoosh. You can also switch weapon and grenade type from the pause menu, with its buttons or with Q and X.

    Keyboard. Left and right arrows turn. Down arrow is about face. Hold Space to fire. L turns Fire lock on and off. R reloads. Q switches weapon. C takes cover. G throws a grenade. X switches grenade type. E reads enemy locations. T is status. Escape pauses. In Jungle scavenger, W or the up arrow walks forward, S walks backward, C starts and stops walking on your own, and V reads your surroundings.

    Settings

    Settings

    Announcements

    Menu reader

    For playing with your screen reader off. The Built-in voice reads every menu: touch or drag a finger to hear what is under it, swipe right or left for the next or previous item, and double-tap anywhere to press it. Swipe up or down to change a slider or picker, or to jump between headings. Drag two fingers to scroll. You can also turn it on or off in any menu by holding two fingers still on the screen for two seconds. The battle screen is not changed.

    Background ambience

    Difficulty

    Enemy health callouts

    Reload callouts

    On iPhone, the game sound drops every time the Built-in voice speaks, and stays low for about a second after. Sounds keeps reloads from cutting your gunfire off.

    Game sound with the Built-in voice

    Only matters on iPhone and iPad with Announcements set to Built-in voice. If the game goes silent on Shared, check that Silent Mode is off, or the ring switch is set to ring.

    Vibration

    Works on Android phones. iPhone browsers do not let web pages vibrate.

    3D audio (headphones)

    With 3D audio on, each sound is shaped the way your ears hear it from that direction, so a zombie behind you really sounds behind you. Long sounds, like a boss roar or Gravemoor's bell, stay where they are and move around your head as you turn. It needs headphones or earbuds; on the phone speaker it sounds about the same as Off. In a huge horde, the quieter sounds fall back to regular stereo to keep the game smooth.

    Graphics

    Only changes the picture in the battle view, for sighted players. Sounds and gameplay are exactly the same either way. Regular zombies and runners are Kenney's free zombie art either way: a flat 2D cartoon zombie in Original, and an animated 3D zombie in Enhanced that shambles, lunges to grab you, flinches when shot and falls to its knees and onto its face when it dies. Enhanced also adds soft shadows under every figure, glowing eyes, glows on burning, shocked and frozen enemies, sparks and dust when you hit something, bigger explosions with smoke, embers, flying debris, a shockwave and a flash of light, a skyline around each map, and weather like snow, fireflies, falling leaves and mist. It adds no extra blood. If your phone starts to slow down, Enhanced quietly uses fewer effects until it runs smoothly again.

    Crosshair

    Only changes the picture in the battle view, for sighted players. Pixel crosshairs from Kenney's Desert Shooter Pack. They turn red on lock-on, like the classic one.
